title: Separated inertia and separated diagonal of a DM stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces and $2$-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a morphism representable by algebraic spaces, separated means that on every scheme base change its algebraic-space diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], tested on scheme charts. Let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $S$. Its inertia $I_{\mathcal X}$ has objects $(x,\alpha)$ over $T$, where $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(x)$, and arrows $v$ satisfying $v\alpha=\beta v$; its projection $p:I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$ forgets the automorphism. Let $e:\mathcal X\to I_{\mathcal X}$ send $x$ to $(x,1_x)$. The following are equivalent: $p$ is separated; the representable diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is separated; and $e$ is a closed immersion. Closed immersion of a representable stack map means a closed immersion of schemes on every scheme base change. This holds also for the underlying stack over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, so that $p$ is separated if and only if $\Delta_{\mathcal X/\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}$ is separated.

proof.text: The DM atlas is a smooth surjective atlas because every representable etale map is smooth [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-inertia-second-diagonal-geometry] to $\mathcal X\to S$. It gives representability of $p$ and of $q=\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$, and identifies $\Delta_q$ with $e$. The scheme-test definition of separatedness of a representable map $q:A\to B$ is equivalent to closedness of $\Delta_q$: for a scheme $T\to A\times_B A$, its two objects and their comparison over $B$ define two sections of $A_T\to T$, where $A_T=T\times_B A$. The pullback of $\Delta_q$ is exactly their equalizer, hence the scheme test of $\Delta_{A_T/T}$ along this pair. Conversely every scheme test of $\Delta_{A_T/T}$ is a test of $\Delta_q$ by the same description of triples in the $2$-fibre product [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Closed immersion in both descriptions means the same scheme morphism is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $q$ is separated if and only if $e$ is a closed immersion.

proof.text: Fix a scheme $T$ and $x\in\mathcal X(T)$. Unpack [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: the base change $G=T\times_{\mathcal X}I_{\mathcal X}$ is the sheaf $\operatorname{Aut}(x)$, an algebraic space by step 1. Explicitly $(y,\beta,v:y\xrightarrow{\sim}x)$ goes to $v\beta v^{-1}$; its inverse sends $g$ to $(x,g,1_x)$. The comparison $v$ gives the natural isomorphism to the original triple, and arrows are uniquely determined by $v$. Composition and inverse of automorphisms give the group operations on $G$, naturally in all $T$-schemes. For a scheme map $a:V\to I_{\mathcal X}$ represented by $(y,\alpha)$, the $2$-fibre product $V\times_{I_{\mathcal X}}\mathcal X$ along $e$ is the subfunctor of $V$ where $\alpha=1_y$: an object is an isomorphism $w:z\xrightarrow{\sim}y$ with $w=\alpha w$, forcing $\alpha=1_y$. When this holds $(z,w)=(y,1_y)$ is an object and the unique arrow between two choices is $w_2^{-1}w_1$. These identifications commute with every further scheme base change.

proof.text: Assume $p$ separated. For an arbitrary scheme test $a:T\to I_{\mathcal X}$ given by $(x,\alpha)$, the algebraic space $G=\operatorname{Aut}(x)$ of step 2 is separated over $T$ by the definition of separatedness of $p$. Thus $\Delta_{G/T}$ is a closed immersion. The two sections $(\alpha,1_x)$ give a scheme map $T\to G\times_TG$, where the product exists by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its pullback of $\Delta_{G/T}$ is the identity locus $\alpha=1_x$, so is a scheme closed in $T$ by the scheme-test meaning of closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Step 2 identifies this actual scheme over $T$ with $T\times_{I_{\mathcal X}}\mathcal X$. This proves that every scheme test of $e$ is a closed immersion, hence that $e$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), (1)(a) implies (c); spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 06P6 (lemma-group-scheme-separated), forward implication, written directly on arbitrary scheme tests.

proof.text: Conversely assume $e$ is a closed immersion. For every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$ with object $x$, form $G=\operatorname{Aut}(x)$ and $G\times_TG$ as in steps 2 and 3 [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A scheme test $V\to G\times_TG$ is a pair of automorphisms $(g,h)$ of $x|_V$. Send it to the object $(x|_V,g^{-1}h)$ of inertia. By step 2 its pullback of $e$ is the subfunctor of $V$ where $g^{-1}h=1$, or equivalently $g=h$; this is precisely $V\times_{G\times_TG}G$ along $\Delta_{G/T}$. Because $e$ is closed, this is a scheme closed in $V$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The equality holds naturally on every further test scheme, so it identifies morphisms, including nilpotent structure, and not just geometric points. Thus $\Delta_{G/T}$ is a closed immersion and $G\to T$ is separated. As $T\to\mathcal X$ was arbitrary, $p$ is separated. Together with step 1 this gives the three equivalences.

source.place: Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), (1)(c) implies (a); spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 06P6 (lemma-group-scheme-separated), cartesian difference-map square, with its pointwise exercise written out.

proof.text: For the absolute diagonal put $R=\mathcal X\times_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal X$ and $P=\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$. The map $P\to R$ is the $2$-base change of the scheme diagonal $S\to S\times_{\mathbf Z}S$: both specify that the two structural maps agree. Hence it is representable by algebraic spaces, and so is the composite $\mathcal X\to P\to R$, by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Here its first factor is representable by step 1; the scheme diagonal is a map of algebraic spaces. The second diagonal of this composite is again $e$, directly from [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: in $\mathcal X\times_{\Delta,R,\Delta}\mathcal X$ a triple is $(x,y,(u,v))$ with isomorphisms $u,v:x\to y$. Send it to $(x,v^{-1}u)$; the inverse sends $(x,\alpha)$ to $(x,x,(\alpha,1_x))$, and $(1_x,v)$ gives the natural comparison. The second diagonal $(x,x,(1_x,1_x))$ goes to $(x,1_x)$. All automorphisms and their base-scheme tests are unchanged on forgetting $S$, since an object over a scheme supplies its structural map to $S$. The scheme-test argument of step 1 therefore applies to this representable absolute diagonal and gives separatedness exactly when $e$ is closed; steps 3--4 give separatedness exactly when $p$ is separated. This argument needs no separatedness of $S$.
